lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: Toronto's homestand has opened with a thud, and the margin for error is already narrowing. The Maple Leafs fell 3-2 to Utah on Tuesday, a defeat made more galling by Sergei Bobrovsky's 33-save performance and Jack Roslovic's two-goal night. Toronto is 8-7, eighth in the Eastern Conference, five points behind, and has lost two of its last three. William Nylander keeps piling up points, but even he admits the puck has not found his stick often enough; production without possession is a leaky foundation. The injury picture offers hope and worry in equal measure: John Tavares returned to practice and could play Saturday, while Roslovic missed Wednesday's session after taking a knock. Saturday's 7 p.m. meeting with Montreal is the next test - and the Leafs need Tavares back, Roslovic healthy, and far more urgency before this homestand becomes a season-shaping autopsy.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The Blue Jays are no longer chasing October; they are chasing credibility. At 79-83 and second in the AL East, the season's final accounting demands more than cosmetic repairs. Free agency is open, with a Dec. 1 lockout deadline looming - a hard clock for a club weighing trade candidates such as Joe Ryan and possible fits like Steven Kwan and Trevor Megill. The greater pressure sits on Vladimir Guerrero Jr., whose 2026 line drew an F from TSN and leaves his promised 2027 rebound as Toronto's central storyline. The rotation also needs bodies: Max Scherzer and Shane Bieber are free agents, while Cody Ponce's return from a right-knee ACL sprain could matter enormously. Even the farm system offers a pulse, with Jake Cook named an Arizona Fall League All-Star. Watch Toronto's first major move before December's deadline - and whether it adds real depth rather than another headline.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: A promising night turned into a warning flare in Denver. The Raptors were flattened 128-109 by the Nuggets after surrendering a 41-15 third quarter - the sort of collapse that exposes a team's unfinished business more clearly than any standings table. Toronto led 67-64 at halftime, then watched its offense seize up: 5-for-23 shooting and seven turnovers in the decisive period. RJ Barrett supplied 22 points, his seventh 20-point game in eight outings, while Scottie Barnes added 17 points, six rebounds, six assists and three steals. Still, the Raptors have lost three of four since their 3-1 start and sit 4-4, third in the Atlantic, with a one-game skid. The schedule offers no soft landing, and Kawhi Leonard remains out with a knee injury while Nate Bittle is day-to-day with a foot issue. Friday's 8 p.m. visit to Milwaukee will test whether Toronto can answer adversity - or merely repeat it.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: A 27-10 demolition of Philadelphia has pulled Washington back from the ledge, but not yet into the clear. The victory on Nov. 1 left the Commanders 2-4-1, alone in second place in the NFC East and riding a one-game winning streak - a pulse, not a revival. The price has been steep: defensive tackles Daron Payne and Javon Kinlaw are out for the season, while leading receiver Terry McLaurin and top rusher Jacory Croskey-Merritt remain on injured reserve. Jer'Zhan Newton's full practice is welcome news, but this front is being rebuilt on the fly. The trade-deadline debate is no longer abstract; Washington must decide whether one impressive Sunday justifies spending for a battered roster. Sunday's 1 p.m. meeting with the Rams will test whether the Eagles win was a turning point or merely a brief escape.
